All other `*AgentTest` suites in the project pass too, confirming the single failure is isolated to the bug found.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/reflect/MethodUtilsAgentTest.java` with 47 self-contained tests covering `MethodUtils`'s method-resolution, annotation, override-hierarchy, and invocation APIs, including boundary/error cases (null/empty args, no-match lookups, private-method access control, varargs, exact vs. loose signature matching, and exception wrapping).

**46 tests pass.** One test fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testGetMatchingMethod_diamondInterfaceAmbiguityThrowsIllegalState`** — exposes a bug in `MethodUtils.getMatchingMethod(Class, String, Class...)`. Its Javadoc states it `@throws IllegalStateException if there is no unique result`, but the implementation only throws when the two best-matching candidates share the same *declaring class*. When a class implements two unrelated interfaces that each independently declare an equally-specific, equally-distant matching method (a classic diamond-inheritance ambiguity), the method silently returns an arbitrary one of them instead of throwing, violating its documented contract.
